knowledge:
- key_parameters: clusters=Used in computeSumFactors() to specify pre-computed quick clusters, reducing sensitivity to violations of the non-DE majority assumption ;; groups=Used in quickSubCluster() to define the parent clusters for nested subclustering ;; subset.row=Used in correlatePairs() to restrict correlation calculations to a specific subset of genes (e.g., top HVGs) ;; block=Used in correlatePairs() to specify a blocking factor (e.g., donor or batch) to prevent uninteresting substructure from driving false correlations
- alternatives: scrapper package=Supersedes most of scran's deprecated/defunct functionality and is recommended for routine single-cell analyses ;; scuttle package=Provides computeSumFactors(), which is used in conjunction with scran's quickCluster()
- when_to_use: Use when performing specialized downstream single-cell RNA-seq analyses, such as cluster-based normalization factor calculation, subclustering within existing groups, technical-variance-based PC selection, or identifying gene-gene correlation networks.
- pitfalls: Using scran for routine analyses that have been superseded by scrapper ;; Failing to block on uninteresting factors (like donor) in correlatePairs(), which can lead to strong spurious correlations ;; Insufficient permutation iterations in correlation testing, which can lead to lower-bounded p-values and trigger warnings.

workflows.name: quick_clustering_and_normalization
workflows.intent: Perform quick clustering to assist in cluster-based normalization factor calculation and subsequent subclustering.
input: sce.ready (SingleCellExperiment object containing pre-processed single-cell RNA-seq data)
workflows.stages: 1. Generate quick-and-dirty clusters using quickCluster() ;; 2. Compute size factors within clusters using computeSumFactors() ;; 3. Perform subclustering within identified clusters using quickSubCluster()
workflows.code:
clusters <- quickCluster(sce.ready)
sce.normed <- computeSumFactors(sce.ready, clusters=clusters)
summary(sizeFactors(sce.normed))
subout <- quickSubCluster(sce.ready, groups=clusters)
table(metadata(subout)$subcluster)

workflows.name: automated_pc_selection
workflows.intent: Determine the optimal number of principal components (PCs) to retain based on technical variance estimates.
input: sce.ready (SingleCellExperiment object with PCA and row metadata containing variance statistics)
workflows.stages: 1. Extract variance explained and technical/total variance statistics ;; 2. Determine the number of PCs to retain using denoisePCANumber() ;; 3. Subset the PCA coordinates to the chosen number of PCs
workflows.code:
var.explained <- metadata(sce.ready)$PCA$variance.explained
stats <- rowData(sce.ready)
total.tech.var.in.hvgs <- sum(stats[stats$hvg,"fitted"])
total.var.in.hvgs <- sum(stats[stats$hvg,"variances"])
chosen <- denoisePCANumber(var.explained, total.tech.var.in.hvgs, total.var.in.hvgs)
chosen
reducedDim(sce.ready, "PCA.denoised") <- reducedDim(sce.ready, "PCA")[,1:chosen]

workflows.name: gene_correlation_analysis
workflows.intent: Identify significant pairwise and gene-level correlations among highly variable genes (HVGs) while blocking on uninteresting batch effects.
input: sce.ready (SingleCellExperiment object with residual variance statistics)
workflows.stages: 1. Select top highly variable genes of interest ;; 2. Compute pairwise correlations using correlatePairs() ;; 3. Compute pairwise correlations blocking on batch/donor effects using correlatePairs(..., block=...) ;; 4. Summarize pairwise correlations into gene-level statistics using correlateGenes()
workflows.code:
of.interest <- order(rowData(sce.ready)$residuals, decreasing=TRUE)[1:200]
cor.pairs <- correlatePairs(sce.ready, subset.row=of.interest)
cor.pairs
cor.pairs2 <- correlatePairs(sce.ready, subset.row=of.interest, block=sce.ready$donor)
cor.genes <- correlateGenes(cor.pairs)
cor.genes
